2610.09892.title: Defensive Sufficiency in a Stackelberg Model of AI Security
2610.09892.paper_summary: Feedback from automated testing, human red teaming, and incident response can strengthen an AI system's defenses when discovered failures lead to effective repairs. We study when this feedback process provides sufficient protection and when investing in it is economically worthwhile. We begin by showing that an attack surface composed of finite number of inputs is defended with probability 1 if every unresolved attack has a persistent chance of discovery, repairs are effective, and subsequent updates preserve earlier protection. We derive completion-time bounds and extend the analysis to growing attack surfaces, repairs that generalize across related attacks, and multiple discovery mechanisms. These results distinguish eventual protection against each fixed attack from complete protection at a single time. We then formulate a defender-led Stackelberg game in which the defender invests in proactive discovery and reactive repair, anticipating the attacker's choice of search effort. We characterize the least-cost allocation that deters attack and the equilibrium regimes in which the defender funds neither capability, one capability, or both. Numerical experiments illustrate these regimes and show how faster repair can reduce compromise duration without reducing compromise probability.unified theory of performance limits in generative language models.
2610.09892.paper_summary_zh: 自動測試、人為紅隊測試和事件響應的反饋可以增強AI系統的防禦，當發現的失敗導致有效的修復時。我們研究這一反饋過程何時提供足夠的保護，以及何時投資於此在經濟上是值得的。我們首先展示，當每個未解決的攻擊都有持續被發現的機會、修復是有效的，且後續更新保留早期的保護時，由有限數量輸入組成的攻擊面以概率1受到防禦。我們推導完成時間界限，並將分析擴展到增長的攻擊面、跨相關攻擊的修復以及多種發現機制。這些結果區分了對每個固定攻擊的最終保護與在單一時間點的完全保護。我們接著制定了一個由防禦者主導的Stackelberg博弈，在這個博弈中，防禦者投資於主動發現和反應修復，預測攻擊者的搜索努力選擇。我們特徵化了阻止攻擊的最低成本分配以及防禦者資助無能力、一種能力或兩種能力的均衡狀態。數值實驗說明了這些狀態，並展示了更快的修復如何在不降低妥協概率的情況下減少妥協持續時間。
2610.09892.author: Subhabrata Majumdar et.al.
